unit.why: The division continues the deathbed narrative of the tzaddik ('מרן') begun in the previous division. It adds the episode of the tzaddik grasping his beard at the moment of death, and R. Y. of Dombrowa crying out on seeing it.
unit.boundary_note: continues the death-of-the-tzaddik story from the previous division; the funeral continues in the next division

stories.start_quote: והנה אז בעת יציאת נשמתו הקדושה
stories.summary_en: At the tzaddik's death, R. Y. of Dombrowa, son-in-law of R. Moshe of Kozhnitz, sees him grasp his holy beard in his last moment. He cries out that we no longer have a rebbe, because he knew the Kozhnitzer Maggid and his son R. Moshe had done the same at death as a special act of self-sacrifice to God.

quotes: היה להם יחוד בזה למסור נפש לה׳ ברגע האחרונה
tags.why: The dying tzaddik gives his soul over to God at the last moment

quotes: ומיד היה צועק ובוכה ואמר כי אין לנו עוד רבי
tags.why: The onlooker understands the meaning of the gesture from earlier precedent
Relatives of the Kozhnitz dynasty are present or mentioned
The narrator frames the episode as testimony he heard at the time

missing_concepts: grasping the beard at the moment of death as a dynastic deathbed rite
mourning and weeping at a tzaddik's passing
